parsed.main_gap: Neither central extremal claim is proved: the lower-bound induction breaks into unsupported parity/dummy assertions, and the upper-bound strategy is only a conjectural sketch with no cut-count or correctness proof.

errors.description: The crucial lower-bound subcase ends with undefined quantities and unsupported assertions. The dummy multiset need not arise from the required power-of-two initial bins, and no argument establishes the claimed bound on the rest's alternating sum.
The other lower-bound subcase invokes an unproved dyadic lattice dichotomy, although cut locations are arbitrary real numbers. Reverse triangle alone cannot show the union has D at least 1.
errors.quote: the reverse-parity of two equal halves forces the combined \(D(Q)\) to be even with respect to the unit lattice generated by the lowest dyadic, ultimately giving \(D(Q)\le D(P)-1\) or \(D(Q)\ge D(P)+1\)

errors.description: The upper bound is not proved. The proposed pairing construction merely asserts that an arbitrary existing partition can be refined into equal pairs plus length 1 using at most n cuts; no construction or cut-count proof is supplied, and pieces cannot be merged.
errors.quote: but starting from an already partially cut stick the residual number of cuts required is at most \(n\).

parsed.notes: The formula for optimal alternating selection, Lemma A, and the reduction to controlling D are meaningful and mostly correct. However, both decisive bounds remain unproved; numerical checks and statements that a cleaner route or precise construction exists cannot replace those arguments.
